note: Captures for the cassette-loading entry. Governed by 198x/decisions/capturing-published-software.md. Media images are never published or committed; the source paths below are local.
framing: FULL RASTER, 352x296, nearest-neighbour x2 — deliberately NOT cropped to the 256x192 picture the way other Vault captures are. The striped border IS the subject here: it is the loading routine writing the border colour as it decodes pulses. Cropping to the active area would remove the thing the figure exists to show.

captures.claim: A tape load shows its progress in the border, because the loader changes the border colour as it decodes — so the stripe pattern is a direct readout of pulses arriving off the tape.

timeline.basic_load: keyword entry: J, SymbolShift+P, SymbolShift+P, Enter

timeline.comment: mid-load — stripes running, game not yet in

captures.claim: A loading screen is a separate, earlier block: the picture is fully displayed while the game itself is still streaming in behind it, stripes still running.

dump.name: Dizzy - The Ultimate Cartoon Adventure (1987)(Code Masters).tzx

captures.block_structure: Six standard-speed (0x10) blocks: header + BASIC loader, header + 62-byte custom loader, then two headerless data blocks — 6,914 bytes (the loading screen) and 41,803 bytes (the game). Those two sizes are what the caption's timing arithmetic is drawn from.

timeline.basic_load: keyword entry: J, SymbolShift+P, SymbolShift+P, Enter

timeline.comment: screen block in and displayed; main block still loading

captures.caveat: This dump does not complete — see emu198x#872, where the TZX hangs on this very screen and never reaches the title. That does not affect the capture or the claim: the loading screen block demonstrably loads and displays correctly, which is exactly what the figure illustrates. Noted here so nobody later reads the frame as evidence the game ran.
